newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean stocks end higher in shortened session.
newsitem.headline: Chilean stocks end higher in shortened session.

text.p: Chilean stocks bounced back from early losses and ended modestly higher on a flurry of fund buying in a quiet, four-hour trading session.
Brokers looked to next week, after the two-day Fiestas Patrias holidays, for the bourse to rebound after a string of stagnant sessions.
The blue-chip IPSA ended 0.29 percent higher to 97.93 points. The all-share IGPA closed 0.53 percent higher to 5420.49 points on slim volume, brokers said.
Trading ended three hours early, at 1330 EDT/1730 GMT, before the two-day national holiday starting Wednesday.

The market paid little attention to final approval for debt repayment accords between the Central Bank and private institutions Banco de Chile and Banco Internacional, nor to news from London on plans by Regent Kingpin to repurchase shares and warrants in the Regent Kingpin Chile Value Fund.
"The market wasn't even reading the news and is looking to next week," said one broker, who said some of his colleagues traded shares worth a mere 600,000 pesos ($1,500).
Risers included Iansa, up 1.4 percent to 90.25 pesos, and Oro Blanco, up 1.8 percent to 2.85 pesos, up from its recent slide.
Masisa slipped 2.3 percent to 194.5 pesos and was the day's steepest decliner. Endesa dipped 0.1 percent to 258.25 pesos, though electrical stocks were mixed.
Brokers expect news from a series of shareholder meetings and the first third quarter earnings reports to start lifting the market as of early October.
Trading on Friday will also be abbreviated, closing at local 1330 EDT/1730 GMT.
